title: Project Quarry — Consolidated Rock Industries Confidential Information Memorandum
summary: Harris Williams & Co. sell-side CIM for Consolidated Rock Industries ("CRI"), a founder-led regional aggregates producer operating 14 permitted quarry sites across Utah, Nevada, Colorado, and Idaho. CRI produces crushed stone, construction sand & gravel, ready-mix concrete, and industrial minerals. LTM Q1'19 revenue of $245M, Adj. EBITDA of $44M (18.0% margin), with an asking EV of ~$350M (7.9x LTM EBITDA). The investment thesis centers on an irreplaceable permitted reserve base (~580M tons, 30+ years of production), structural supply constraints from permitting barriers, strong pricing power (#1–2 position in 6 MSAs), vertical integration via owned fleet and ready-mix operations, and a proven roll-up strategy with an active bolt-on pipeline. CEO David Mercer, the founder with 62% equity, is leading a transition via a targeted sale process with IOIs due April 5, 2019.

growth_drivers: Irreplaceable permitted reserve base with 30+ year production horizon
Infrastructure tailwind from IIJA ($550B+ in construction spending through 2028)
Strong pricing power — 20% ASP premium over regional average due to permit scarcity
Vertically integrated operations with owned 220-vehicle fleet and ready-mix division
Active bolt-on M&A pipeline — 6 targets identified, 3 in late-stage negotiation (~$85M combined EV)
Western US population growth and supply-constrained permitting environment
risks: Founder dependency — CEO David Mercer owns 62% equity and is central to strategy
Cyclicality tied to construction activity (residential, commercial, infrastructure)
Customer concentration — top 20 accounts represent 58% of revenue, managed by single VP Sales
Regulatory/permitting exposure — new quarry permitting takes 8–15 years in Mountain West
Commodity exposure — aggregate pricing sensitive to regional supply/demand dynamics
Integration risk from active roll-up acquisition strategy

title: Project Quarry — Executive Teaser

key_quotes.quote: With over 580M tons of permitted mineral reserves, CRI offers an acquiror 30+ years of fully-permitted production capacity — a near-irreplaceable asset given increasingly restrictive permitting environments.
Crushed stone ASP of $14.20/ton vs. regional average $11.80/ton — 20% premium reflects permit scarcity · Pricing increased 6.2% in FY2018 with no volume impact.
CEO David Mercer has identified 6 bolt-on quarry targets in adjacent markets (WY, MT, AZ) · 3 targets in late-stage negotiation; combined EV ~$85M at 5–6x EBITDA (immediate accretion).
